_doc: Italy, written by hand for the recommended trips (Manu, 2026-11-16: 'come se potessero andare già in production'). Zones as tour operators sleep in them; seasons from the sources (lifts and huts of the Dolomites, the boats of the Aeolian and Amalfi coasts). Scores on docs/RANKING.md.

areas.season: Best April to early June and late September to October. July and August are 33-35 °C in the afternoon; winter is mild (12-14 °C by day) with rain in November and December.
areas.sleep: Centro Storico or Monti, on foot to the Forum and the Pantheon; Trastevere for the evenings; Prati near the Vatican for quiet.

items.name: Colosseum, Roman Forum and the Palatine
items.book: Colosseum timed tickets sell out weeks ahead in spring
items.why: The arena of 50,000, then the Forum where Rome was run and the hill of the emperors' palaces above it.

steps.note: the ticket covers Forum and Palatine for 24 hours

steps.what: Down into the Roman Forum: Via Sacra, the Curia, the Arch of Titus

items.name: Vatican Museums, Sistine Chapel and St Peter's
items.book: Vatican Museums online, a week or more ahead
items.why: Michelangelo's ceiling, Raphael's rooms and the biggest church in the world; shoulders and knees covered.

steps.note: closed Sundays except the last of the month

steps.what: St Peter's Basilica and, for the fit, the 551 steps of the dome

items.name: Pantheon, Piazza Navona and the Trevi Fountain
items.why: The 2,000-year-old dome, the Baroque square and the fountain, linked by the lanes of the old centre.

steps.what: Piazza Navona and Campo de' Fiori
Trevi Fountain and the Spanish Steps at golden hour

items.name: Galleria Borghese and the Villa Borghese park
items.why: Bernini's marble that looks like skin, in a villa in Rome's central park.

steps.what: Pincio terrace over Piazza del Popolo

items.name: Appian Way and the catacombs by bike
items.why: The Roman road paved 2,300 years ago, between tombs and pines, and the underground cemeteries of the first Christians.

steps.what: Rent a bike at the Appia Antica park office
Ride the old paving to the tomb of Cecilia Metella

rain.name: Museums: Capitoline and Vatican
rain.why: The Capitoline Museums and the Vatican are both indoors, with the Forum seen from the windows.

extras: Fountains (nasoni) give free drinking water all over the city.
Churches want shoulders and knees covered: a light scarf does it.

areas.season: April-June and September-October. July and August are among Italy's hottest (35 °C in the basin). Winter is cool, 10 °C by day, few crowds.
areas.sleep: Inside the centre, between the Duomo and Santa Croce; Oltrarno across the river for a quieter stay.

items.name: The Duomo, Brunelleschi's dome and the Baptistery
items.book: Dome climb on a fixed slot, book ahead
items.why: 463 steps up inside the biggest brick dome ever built, past the Last Judgement painted under it.

steps.what: Climb of the dome, booked slot
Giotto's bell tower for the view of the dome

items.name: The Uffizi
items.why: Botticelli's Venus and Spring, Leonardo, Raphael, Caravaggio: the Renaissance in one corridor.

steps.what: Piazza della Signoria and the Palazzo Vecchio

items.name: Ponte Vecchio, Oltrarno and Piazzale Michelangelo
items.why: Across the goldsmiths' bridge to the artisans' side, then up to the terrace for sunset over the domes.

steps.what: Santo Spirito and the workshops of Oltrarno
Up the steps to San Miniato and Piazzale Michelangelo for sunset

items.name: Michelangelo's David at the Accademia
items.why: Five metres of marble, the most famous statue in the world, seen from all sides.

items.name: Day out to Pisa and Lucca
items.why: The leaning tower and its white square, then a ride on Lucca's walls, a ring of trees around a whole town.

steps.what: Piazza dei Miracoli: tower, cathedral, baptistery

rain.name: Palazzo Pitti and the Bargello
rain.why: Two indoor collections for a wet day: the Medici palace and Florence's sculpture museum.

extras: Many museums close on Mondays: plan the walks for that day.

areas.season: April-June and September-October. July-August hot and crowded; November-January brings acqua alta (high water) on some mornings and fog, but empty lanes.
areas.sleep: In Venice itself, not in Mestre: Cannaregio or Castello for the quiet, near a vaporetto stop.

items.name: St Mark's Basilica, the Doge's Palace and the Grand Canal
items.why: The golden mosaics of the basilica, the palace of the doges and its prisons, then the Grand Canal on vaporetto line 1.

steps.what: Doge's Palace and the Bridge of Sighs
Lunch of cicchetti at a bacaro near Rialto
Vaporetto line 1 down the Grand Canal at sunset

items.name: Lost in Cannaregio and Castello
items.why: The Venice of washing lines and quiet canals, the old Jewish Ghetto and the Arsenale's shipyard walls.

steps.what: The Ghetto, the first in the world
Fondamenta della Misericordia for a spritz

items.name: Murano, Burano and Torcello
items.why: Glass furnaces on Murano, the coloured houses of Burano and the 7th-century mosaics of Torcello in the lagoon.

steps.what: Vaporetto from Fondamente Nove to Murano

items.name: Gallerie dell'Accademia and the Guggenheim
items.why: Titian and Tintoretto, then Peggy Guggenheim's modern art on the Grand Canal.

rain.name: Scuola Grande di San Rocco
rain.why: Tintoretto covered every wall and ceiling of it; the best indoor hour in Venice.

extras: A day pass for the vaporetto pays for itself after three rides.
On certain spring and summer days a day-tripper access fee applies: check before you go.

areas.season: April-June and September-October; the Palio horse race fills the Campo on 2 July and 16 August. Winter is quiet and grey, 10 °C.
areas.sleep: Inside Siena's walls, or a farmhouse (agriturismo) in the Val d'Orcia with a car.

items.name: Piazza del Campo, the Duomo and the Torre del Mangia
items.why: The shell-shaped square, the striped cathedral with its marble floor, and 400 steps up the tower.

steps.what: Siena Cathedral and its Piccolomini Library

items.name: Val d'Orcia: Pienza, Montepulciano and the cypress roads
items.why: The rolling hills and lines of cypresses of every Tuscany poster, with pecorino in Pienza and Vino Nobile in Montepulciano.

steps.what: Wine tasting and lunch in Montepulciano
The cypresses of San Quirico and the chapel of Vitaleta

items.name: San Gimignano and the Chianti
items.why: The medieval town of towers, then the vineyard roads between Florence and Siena.

steps.what: Lunch and tasting in a Chianti winery

rain.name: Santa Maria della Scala
rain.why: The old hospital across from the Duomo, frescoed wards and the city museum.

extras: The Val d'Orcia needs a car; buses exist but are rare.

areas.season: May-June and September-October. July-August hot and very busy. November-March the boats stop, some paths close after storms, many restaurants shut.
areas.sleep: In one of the villages (Monterosso has the beach) or in La Spezia, 10 minutes by train.

items.name: The Blue Path: Monterosso to Vernazza to Corniglia
items.book: Cinque Terre Card (trail fee); check path status after rain
items.why: The cliff path between the colourful villages, with vineyards above and the sea below.

steps.what: Start in Monterosso before the heat and the crowds
steps.note: Cinque Terre Card for the path

steps.what: Vernazza, swim or coffee in the harbour

items.name: The five villages by train and boat
items.why: Riomaggiore and Manarola by train, then the boat along the coast to see them from the sea.

steps.what: Manarola's harbour and the vineyard viewpoint
Lunch, then the boat from Manarola to Monterosso

items.name: Train hops and the sanctuaries above the villages
items.why: In winter the boats stop and the coast path may be shut: the villages are empty and the high paths to the sanctuaries open.

steps.what: Path up to the sanctuary of Reggio

rain.name: La Spezia's naval museum and old town
rain.why: La Spezia is 10 minutes away by train.

extras: The Cinque Terre Express train runs every 15-30 minutes: no car needed, parking is near impossible.

areas.season: Pleasant from March to November; July-August 32 °C. Winter mild and rainy, 13 °C, the best time for the museums.
areas.sleep: In the centro storico near Spaccanapoli, or Chiaia by the sea for a calmer stay.

items.name: Pompeii
items.book: Tickets online, timed in high season
items.why: A whole Roman city buried by Vesuvius in 79 AD: streets, bakeries, frescoed houses and the plaster casts of its people.

steps.what: Circumvesuviana train to Pompei Scavi (40 min)
Gates open, start at the Forum
House of the Vettii and the Lupanar
Amphitheatre and the Garden of the Fugitives

items.name: Spaccanapoli, the underground and pizza
items.why: The street that splits the old town, the veiled Christ of San Severo, Greek-Roman tunnels under the city and pizza where it was born.

steps.what: Sansevero Chapel and the Veiled Christ
Via San Gregorio Armeno, the crib-makers' street

items.name: National Archaeological Museum
items.why: The treasures taken from Pompeii and Herculaneum: mosaics, frescoes and the Farnese marbles.

items.name: Vesuvius crater and Herculaneum
items.book: Vesuvius ticket online, timed; in winter the crater path often shuts for wind and ice
items.why: The walk to the rim of the volcano that buried both towns, then Herculaneum, smaller and better kept than Pompeii.

steps.what: Bus to the Vesuvius car park
30 min up the path to the crater

items.name: Lungomare, Castel dell'Ovo and the Royal Palace
items.why: The bay and Vesuvius from the seafront, the egg castle on its rock and the square of the kings.

steps.what: Piazza del Plebiscito and the Royal Palace

rain.name: Archaeological Museum and Capodimonte
rain.why: Two of Italy's great museums, a day of art under one roof each.

extras: Watch your phone on the Circumvesuviana and in crowded lanes.

areas.season: April to October; July-August hot and full. Sorrento stays open all winter, with fewer boats to Capri and the Amalfi Coast.
areas.sleep: Sorrento centre near Piazza Tasso: buses and ferries leave from there.

items.name: Capri by boat
items.why: Round the island by boat to the grottoes and the Faraglioni rocks, then the piazzetta and the chairlift up Monte Solaro.

steps.note: Blue Grotto only in calm sea

steps.what: Bus to Anacapri, chairlift to Monte Solaro
Gardens of Augustus and Via Krupp viewpoint

items.name: The Amalfi Coast road by bus
items.why: The cliff road from Sorrento to Positano and Amalfi, with the lemon terraces below.

steps.what: SITA bus to Positano (sit on the right)
Bus or boat on to Amalfi, lunch

items.name: Sorrento's old town and the Marina Grande
items.why: Limoncello shops, the cloister of San Francesco and the fishermen's harbour for dinner.

steps.what: Villa Comunale terrace over the bay

items.name: Swim at the Bagni della Regina Giovanna
items.why: A pool of clear sea inside the ruins of a Roman villa, 30 minutes' walk from town.

steps.what: Walk out along Capo di Sorrento

rain.name: Herculaneum or Pompeii from Sorrento
rain.why: The Circumvesuviana train reaches both from Sorrento.

extras: Positano and Amalfi close many hotels from November to March; Sorrento does not.

areas.season: May-June and September-October. July-August crowded and hot; many hotels and boats close November to March.
areas.sleep: Amalfi town or Positano: buses and boats from both. Ravello for quiet.

items.name: The Path of the Gods
items.why: The path high above the coast from Bomerano to Nocelle, with Positano and Capri below.

steps.what: Nocelle, then 1,700 steps down to Positano

items.name: Ravello's villas and Amalfi town
items.why: The gardens of Villa Rufolo and Villa Cimbrone hanging 350 m above the sea, then Amalfi's cathedral.

steps.what: Back down to Amalfi for lunch

items.name: The coast by boat
items.why: Coves, grottoes and swims you only reach from the sea, between Amalfi and Positano.

rain.name: The Paper Museum in Amalfi
rain.why: Amalfi's medieval paper mills, still working.

extras: The coast road has one lane each way and buses fill up: leave early.

areas.season: All year for food; spring and autumn best. Foggy in winter, hot in summer, with 40 km of arcades for shade and rain.
areas.sleep: Inside the ring, near Piazza Maggiore or the university quarter.

items.name: Piazza Maggiore, the towers and the arcades
items.why: The red city of arcades, the leaning towers and the market lanes of the Quadrilatero.

steps.what: Walk the arcades up to San Luca

items.name: Modena and Parma food day
items.book: Dairy and acetaia visits by booking
items.why: Balsamic vinegar in Modena's attics, then Parmigiano and Parma ham where they are made.

rain.name: The arcades themselves
rain.why: Bologna's porticoes keep you dry across the whole centre.

areas.season: April-October; opera in the Arena from June to early September. Winter cold and foggy, Christmas market in December.
areas.sleep: Inside the old town between the Arena and the Adige.

items.name: The Arena, Juliet's balcony and the old town
items.why: A Roman amphitheatre still used for opera, the market square and the hill of Castel San Pietro over the river.

steps.what: Piazza delle Erbe and Juliet's house
Funicular or steps to Castel San Pietro for sunset

items.name: An opera night in the Arena
items.book: Seats sell out; stone steps are cheapest
items.why: Aida under the stars with 15,000 people, in a theatre built in the year 30.

items.name: Valpolicella wineries
items.why: Amarone made from dried grapes, in the hills 20 minutes away.

areas.season: Spring and autumn best; humid and hot in July, many shops shut in mid-August; cold and foggy winter.
areas.sleep: Near the Duomo or in Brera; Navigli for the evenings.

items.name: The Duomo roof and the Galleria
items.why: A forest of marble spires you can walk among, then the glass arcade of the Galleria Vittorio Emanuele.

items.name: Leonardo's Last Supper and Brera
items.book: Last Supper tickets open months ahead and sell out
items.why: Fifteen minutes before the most famous wall in the world, then the Brera gallery and its quarter.

items.name: Navigli canals at aperitivo time
items.why: The old canals of Milan, where the city goes for the evening spritz.

areas.season: April-October; gardens bloom in April-May. Many boats and villas close November to March, and the lake is often grey.
areas.sleep: Varenna or Bellagio in the middle of the lake, where the ferries cross.

items.name: Bellagio, Varenna and Villa Carlotta by ferry
items.why: The triangle of villages in the middle of the lake and the gardens of Villa Carlotta, all linked by ferry.

steps.what: Ferry to Bellagio, its stepped lanes

items.name: Greenway del Lago and Villa del Balbianello
items.why: A lakeside path between old villages to the villa on its peninsula from Star Wars and Casino Royale.

steps.note: closed Mondays and Wednesdays; winter shut

items.name: Castello di Vezio above Varenna
items.why: A short climb through olive trees to the tower over the lake, then the waterfront walk at dusk.

areas.season: April-October; windsurf wind in the north every afternoon; mild for the Alps' foot even in March and November.
areas.sleep: Sirmione or Malcesine; Riva del Garda for hikes and bikes.

items.name: Sirmione's castle and the Grottoes of Catullus
items.why: A moated castle on the water and a Roman villa at the tip of the peninsula.

items.name: Across the lake by ferry
items.why: Limone's lemon houses and the northern shore between mountains.

items.name: Monte Baldo cable car from Malcesine
items.why: A rotating cable car to 1,760 m, with the whole lake below and walks on the ridge.

areas.season: All year: a base for the Dolomites, a famous Christmas market (late November to early January), 30 °C in July.
areas.sleep: Old town near Piazza Walther.

items.name: Ötzi the Iceman and the old town
items.why: The 5,300-year-old man found in the ice, then the arcades and Tyrolean taverns of the old town.

steps.note: closed Mondays except July-August and December

steps.what: Lauben arcades and the fruit market

items.name: Renon plateau and the earth pyramids
items.why: Cable car and narrow-gauge tram to the plateau, then a walk to the earth pillars with the Dolomites behind.

areas.season: Summer hiking mid-June to late September, when the lifts and huts open. Skiing December to March (Dolomiti Superski). April-May and October-November most lifts are shut.
areas.sleep: Ortisei for the village life, Selva for the lifts.

items.name: Seceda ridge
items.why: The saw-tooth ridge of the Odle seen from the top of the Seceda lift, then down through alpine meadows and huts.

steps.what: Cable car from Ortisei to Seceda

items.name: Alpe di Siusi
items.why: Europe's biggest high meadow under the Sassolungo and the Sciliar, flat enough for everyone.

steps.what: Cable car from Ortisei to Alpe di Siusi

items.name: Round the Sassolungo
items.why: The full loop around the great tooth of the valley from Passo Sella, 17 km among scree and huts.

items.name: Ski the Sella Ronda
items.book: Dolomiti Superski pass; ski hire in Selva
items.why: A day on skis round the Sella massif through four valleys, without skiing the same run twice.

steps.what: Lunch at a hut on the way

items.name: Winter walks and sledging on Alpe di Siusi
items.why: Groomed snow paths and toboggan runs on the high meadow, for those not on skis.

steps.what: Lunch at a hut, sledge down

items.name: Ortisei and its woodcarvers
items.why: The village of the Ladin woodcarvers, its pedestrian street and the museum of the valley.

rain.name: Museum Gherdëina in Ortisei
rain.why: The valley's woodcarving, the Ladin language and the first climbers.

extras: The Val Gardena Mobil Card (with some stays) covers buses and trains in South Tyrol.

areas.season: Summer hiking mid-June to September; skiing December to March. In October-November and April-May many lifts and huts shut.
areas.sleep: Cortina itself, or Dobbiaco for the Tre Cime and Braies.

items.name: Round the Tre Cime di Lavaredo
items.book: Auronzo road toll by booking in summer
items.why: The three great rock towers of the Dolomites, round on a 10 km path from the Auronzo hut.

steps.what: Drive or bus to the Auronzo hut
Path to Rifugio Lavaredo and the Forcella

items.name: Lago di Braies
items.book: Summer access by booked parking or shuttle
items.why: The emerald lake under the cliffs of the Croda del Becco, walked round in an hour.

steps.what: Arrive early: the road is limited in summer

items.name: Cinque Torri and the open-air WWI museum
items.why: Five rock towers with the trenches of the First World War between them, reached by chairlift.

items.name: Ski Cortina and the Lagazuoi
items.why: Cortina's Olympic slopes and the long run from the Lagazuoi to Armentarola, pulled by horses at the end.

items.name: Corso Italia and the Olympic town
items.why: The pedestrian street of the queen of the Dolomites, its bell tower and the 1956 Olympic ice stadium.

extras: Some huts and lifts close for a few weeks between seasons: check opening dates.

areas.season: Mild all year: 15 °C by day in winter, 31 °C in July-August. Best April-June and September-October.
areas.sleep: Around the Quattro Canti or Kalsa, on foot to everything.

items.name: Norman Palace, the Cathedral and the markets
items.why: Golden Arab-Norman mosaics in the Palatine Chapel, the cathedral, and street food at the Ballarò market.

steps.what: Kalsa quarter and the sea front

items.name: Monreale cathedral
items.why: 6,400 square metres of gold mosaic in a cathedral above the city, and its cloister of 228 columns.

items.name: Mondello beach
items.why: Palermo's white-sand bay under Monte Pellegrino.

items.name: Street food walk at dusk
items.why: Vucciria and the old harbour when Palermo comes out for the evening.

rain.name: Palazzo Abatellis and the Salinas museum
rain.why: Medieval Sicily's art and its archaeology, indoors.

extras: Shops and some sites shut 13:00-16:00: plan the markets for the morning.

areas.season: April-October for the islands; mild winters (14 °C). The Egadi boats run all year, fewer in winter.
areas.sleep: Trapani's old town on its spit of land.

items.name: Erice and the salt pans at sunset
items.why: The medieval town on its mountain by cable car, then the windmills of the salt pans in the evening light.

steps.what: Castle of Venus and the stone lanes
Salt pans of Nubia at sunset

items.name: Favignana by bike
items.why: Hydrofoil to the butterfly island, then bike to Cala Rossa and Bue Marino for the clearest sea of Sicily.

steps.what: Bue Marino and the tuna factory

items.name: Segesta temple and theatre
items.why: A Greek temple standing alone in the hills since the 5th century BC.

steps.what: Temple, then up to the theatre

areas.season: All year; hot in summer, so the temples at opening or sunset.
areas.sleep: Agrigento's old town or a farmhouse near the Valley.

items.name: Valley of the Temples
items.best: Opening or the evening opening in summer
items.why: Seven Doric temples on a ridge over the sea, the Temple of Concordia as whole as in 430 BC.

steps.what: Gates open, start at the Temple of Juno

items.name: Scala dei Turchi
items.why: A white marl cliff stepped like a staircase into the sea.

items.name: Villa Romana del Casale
items.why: The richest Roman mosaics in the world, the girls in bikinis among them, on the way to the east coast.

areas.season: All year; the Baroque towns are at their best in the low sun of spring and autumn.
areas.sleep: Ragusa Ibla, the lower old town.

items.name: Ragusa Ibla and Modica's chocolate
items.why: Two Baroque towns rebuilt after the 1693 earthquake on gorges, and chocolate made the Aztec way.

steps.what: Steps down from Ragusa Superiore to Ibla

items.name: Noto, the stone garden
items.why: A whole town of golden Baroque churches and palaces, and its almond granita.

steps.what: Cathedral and the balconies of Palazzo Nicolaci

items.name: Marina di Ragusa and the Vendicari reserve
items.why: Sandy beaches and a coastal reserve with flamingos in winter.

areas.season: Mild all year; swimming May to October. The Greek theatre stages classical plays May-July.
areas.sleep: Ortigia, the island old town.

items.name: Neapolis: the Greek theatre and the Ear of Dionysius
items.why: One of the biggest Greek theatres and the cave whose echo let a tyrant hear his prisoners.

items.name: Ortigia: the Duomo and the market
items.why: A cathedral built into a Greek temple, the morning market and the sea all around the old town.

steps.what: Sunset passeggiata on the sea walls

items.name: Boat round Ortigia and swim
items.why: Sea caves under the old town, then a swim off the rocks.

items.name: A Greek tragedy in the Greek theatre
items.why: The plays performed where they were written for, 2,500 years on.

areas.season: April-October; Etna's summit is snowy November-April and cold at the top all year.
areas.sleep: Taormina on its terrace; Giardini Naxos below for the beach.

items.name: Mount Etna in the snow
items.why: Europe's highest active volcano under snow: the Silvestri craters at 1,900 m, black lava against white, the sea below.

steps.what: Drive or tour to Rifugio Sapienza (1.5 h)
steps.note: chains or a tour in snow

steps.what: Etna winery on the way down

items.name: Mount Etna's craters
items.book: Upper zone with an authorised guide
items.why: Europe's highest active volcano: the Silvestri craters, the cable car to 2,500 m and lava fields still warm in places.

steps.what: Drive or tour to Rifugio Sapienza (1.5 h)
Cable car to 2,500 m, 4x4 bus or guided walk to 2,900 m
steps.note: the summit only with an authorised guide

steps.what: Etna winery on the way down

items.name: Taormina: the Greek theatre and Corso Umberto
items.why: A Greek-Roman theatre with Etna and the sea as its stage set, and the town's balcony streets.

steps.what: Corso Umberto and Piazza IX Aprile at sunset

items.name: Isola Bella and the coast below
items.why: Cable car down to the pebble cove and the islet, then a boat to the Blue Grotto.

items.name: Alcantara gorge
items.why: Basalt columns of an old lava flow cut by an icy river.

steps.what: Gorge, waders to walk in the river in summer

areas.season: May-October; ferries and hydrofoils are few from November to March and the islands go to sleep.
areas.sleep: Lipari town: every boat to the other islands leaves from there.

items.name: Stromboli at night
items.why: The volcano that has erupted every few minutes for 2,000 years, seen at dusk from the sea or from 400 m on the authorised path.

steps.note: higher only with a guide when allowed

steps.what: Boat by the Sciara del Fuoco to watch the eruptions

items.name: Vulcano's crater
items.why: Up the Gran Cratere in an hour, sulphur fumaroles at the top and four islands in view.

steps.what: Climb the crater before the heat
Black sand beach with hot springs in the sea

items.name: Salina and Lipari by boat
items.why: The green island of capers and Malvasia wine, Pollara's cliff beach, and swims in the coves of Lipari.

items.name: Lipari castle and town
items.why: The acropolis on its rock and the museum of the islands' 6,000 years.

areas.season: All year; beach May-October.
areas.sleep: Old town under the rock.

items.name: The Norman cathedral and the old town
items.why: A Norman cathedral with a golden Christ Pantocrator, the old wash-house and the town's beach under the rock.

items.name: La Rocca
items.why: The rock over the town, with a temple of Diana and the coast below.

steps.what: Temple of Diana and castle ruins

areas.season: All year; spring and autumn best. Hot in July-August, cold winter evenings (3 °C).
areas.sleep: A cave hotel in the Sassi.

items.name: The Sassi and the rock churches
items.why: A town carved into a ravine and lived in for 9,000 years, its frescoed cave churches and a furnished cave house.

steps.what: Santa Maria de Idris and San Pietro Barisano

items.name: Across the ravine to the Murgia
items.why: Down to the river on the rope bridge and up to the cave churches facing the town.

steps.what: Back for the lit town at night

areas.season: April-October; mild winters. A car makes the valley.
areas.sleep: A trullo in Alberobello, or a masseria (farm) in the Valle d'Itria.

items.name: The trulli of Alberobello
items.why: A town of white stone houses with cone roofs, painted with symbols.

steps.what: Rione Monti before the tour buses

items.name: Locorotondo, Cisternino and Ostuni
items.why: White towns on hilltops over a valley of trulli and olive trees, butcher-grills in Cisternino, and Ostuni, the white city.

steps.what: Cisternino: choose your meat, they grill it

items.name: Castellana caves
items.why: 3 km of caverns ending in the white Grotta Bianca.

areas.season: Swimming June-September; the towns are lively from Easter to October.
areas.sleep: Polignano's old town on the cliff.

items.name: Lama Monachile and the cliff town
items.why: A pebble cove between cliffs under the old town, balconies over the sea.

items.name: Monopoli and the coves to the south
items.why: A working harbour of blue boats and the little rocky coves below the town.

areas.season: Beaches June-September; Lecce's Baroque is lovely all year. August is crowded with Italian holidays.
areas.sleep: Lecce's old town; a masseria near the coast in summer.

items.name: Lecce's Baroque
